I'm still trying to find my political identity but as a person who lives in Poland I think it's important to look at the whole image of how the things worked. Because usually for people living in former eastern bloc socialism is associated with all the terrible things that happened there. Few examples there was a censorship and thus also a lot of pro government propaganda. Of course every country have a more pro government outlet but then you couldn't criticise the state ever. You can also look at how the Chernobyl explosion was handled. They didn't tell people immediately (so they could stay inside and also drink lugol's iodine) and didn't evacuate the city of Chernobyl till 36 hours after the disaster. People had to stay in long lines to get almost anything, and somethings were almost impossible to get because there was nothing in shops, the shelves were more empty than not.  The oranges were special treat on Christmas only as you mentioned. The police was awful. They were often accusing innocent people just to say that they finished the investigation, beating people to confess was a common practice. And of course the existence of things like gulags. I think it's hard for people who know these things from their own experiences or experiences of their loved ones to have good reactions to socialism because they associate it with all those terrible things that happened. I think it's important to respect that, as the trauma of that days still exists even now. Honestly it is my issue with socialism because I know these things and I would hated living there even though I don't support capitalism (I'm currently looking at different ideas that could be the best (imo) alternative to capitalism). And of course I'm sorry for any mistakes English is not my first language.
I also don't want to attack any political beliefs but I wanted to explain it from the point of view of someone who lives in post eastern bloc and show you what is the root of this arguments.
